strengths: The paper addresses an important question: how adversarial training can preserve clean generalization while achieving low robust training error and poor robust test performance. The separate definitions of these errors make the objective clear.

Partial signal learning combined with training-noise memorization provides an interpretable candidate mechanism. Connecting representation complexity with learning dynamics is a potentially useful contribution.
Experiments include MNIST, CIFAR10, synthetic feature-learning trajectories, and input-loss flatness measurements. These offer several complementary ways to investigate the proposed mechanism.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under its stated assumptions. Consider uniform data at ±e1, labeled ±1, with δ=1/4. The polynomial-size ReLU classifier f_clean(x)=x1−8|x2| satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3: clean error is zero and robust error is 1/2. With N growing polynomially in D, both atoms have substantial empirical frequency with high probability. Consequently, o(1) robust training error forces robustness at both atoms and hence zero robust test error, making a CGRO classifier impossible. Additional assumptions controlling distributional mass and sample coverage are necessary.

The representation proof has further substantive gaps. Assumption 4.2 separates opposite classes; it does not imply disjoint perturbation balls around same-class samples, as asserted in Lemma 4.5. The resulting rewrite using a sum of indicators is therefore generally invalid. Appendix F also claims uniform o(1) approximation of a potentially discontinuous classifier by continuous ReLU networks. Softening indicators cannot establish this uniform approximation, and classification guarantees require explicit control of transition regions and margins.

Theorem 5.9 does not establish the stated robust training guarantee. Definition 5.6 optimizes over perturbations confined to the signal patch and signal direction, whereas Definition 3.3 measures robustness over the entire norm ball. Small loss against the restricted adversary does not imply small full-ball robust training error. The restricted attack can establish a lower bound on robust test error, but the corresponding training-error implication is missing.

The clean-generalization proof in Appendix E.12 incorrectly treats sums of cubic Gaussian projections as sub-Gaussian. Even a single nonzero cubed Gaussian is not sub-Gaussian, so the displayed concentration bound is unjustified. The inference from V_i=Θ(1) to ||β_r||=Θ(1) for every neuron is also unsupported. These steps directly affect the principal clean-generalization conclusion.

The additional generalization bound in Theorem B.1 is also invalid as stated. A constant nonzero predictor has zero input-gradient flatness, while its logistic loss varies with the label. Its empirical loss can underestimate population loss with nonvanishing probability, even for smooth class-conditional densities. The proposed bound has no term accounting for this sampling fluctuation. Appendix G does not justify eliminating its additive density-estimation errors.

The claimed novelty and connection between the two theoretical views need sharper justification. Theorem 4.7 is existential, and Appendix F still constructs linearly separable examples; this does not demonstrate the advertised extension beyond the linear-separable lower bound attributed to Li et al. (2022). Moreover, the worst-case hard distribution is not connected to the structured distribution used for the dynamics analysis, so the representation separation does not establish why that learner follows the proposed trajectory.

The experiments do not resolve these theoretical concerns. Section 6.2 sets δ=α=10, contradicting Assumption 5.7's strict δ<α and allowing complete removal of the signal patch. This materially changes the regime being validated. The manuscript also lacks sufficient PGD settings, attack-strength checks, repeated-run uncertainty, and optimization details for reliable reproduction. Model-size trends and flatness correlations are suggestive, but do not establish the proposed causal mechanism. Substantial theoretical corrections and experiments aligned with the corrected assumptions are needed for acceptance.
